entities.summary: Jerónimo Bécker y González was a Spanish historian, diplomat, and journalist of great significance in the development of modern Spanish historiography. He was born in Salamanca, Spain on December 2, 1857, and died on May 25, 1925. Bécker's work had a profound impact on the understanding of Spanish history, particularly in the fields of diplomacy and international relations. His contributions to the field of historical journalism were instrumental in shaping public opinion on issues of national identity and foreign policy. The establishment of the Spanish Historical Institute in Madrid in 1914, which Bécker co-founded, marked a significant turning point in the development of modern Spanish historiography. The Institute's focus on preserving and promoting Spanish historical knowledge helped to establish the country's rich cultural heritage as a cornerstone of national identity. Bécker's legacy can be seen in the numerous historical journals and publications that continue to be published in Spain today, which owe a debt of gratitude to his pioneering work. Through his tireless efforts to promote Spanish history and culture, Bécker left an enduring mark on the country's intellectual and cultural landscape.
